extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2020 reviewers (and area chairs); volunteer peer reviewers for the NeurIPS conference
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for serving as a reviewer for NeurIPS 2020: duties, expected behavior, and detailed evaluation criteria to use when assessing submitted papers, participating in discussions, and handling author responses. Covers procedural rules (conflicts, confidentiality, double-blind), review form items (summary, strengths, weaknesses, correctness, clarity, prior work, reproducibility, scores), and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities and workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer will be assigned around 4-6 submissions and is responsible for reviewing submissions, reading author responses, discussing submissions and author responses with other reviewers and area chairs (ACs), and helping make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must log in to CMT as soon as notified to check conflicts and expertise; if not comfortable reviewing, fill out a note in CMT and communicate to the AC immediately. Engage actively in the discussion phase for each assigned submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines and respond to emails as promptly as possible; ensure CMT email is not marked as spam and update contact information if it changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam folder regularly and whitelist CMT. Notify ACs if you will be unavailable for more than a few days, especially during important windows (e.g., discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining reviewer profile and conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Log into TPMS and OpenReview to ensure your profile is up to date; make sure domain conflicts in CMT are current to prevent assignment errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a stale profile causes poor assignments; check and update domain conflicts so conflicts during the review process are prevented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest & communication restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not talk to other reviewers, ACs, or SACs about submissions assigned to you without prior approval from your AC; do not talk to reviewers/ACs/SACs about submissions you are an author on or have a conflict with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary contact should be the corresponding AC. If you find a submission not adequately anonymized, contact the corresponding AC. Never attempt to find out authors' identities (e.g., via Google or arXiv); if you accidentally learn identities, do not divulge them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and non-use of ideas/code
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything relating to the review process confidential. Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they become publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not talk about or distribute submissions (code or ideas/results) without program chairs' approval. Code submitted for reviewing cannot be distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the NeurIPS code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants must agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must accord with the code of conduct. Use neutral, non-discriminatory language (e.g., avoid phrasing that implies the author is 'foreign' or 'non-native'); prefer 'Please have your submission proof-read for English style and grammar issues.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs (they cannot see author identities). Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions; reviewers should not attempt to discover identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is not anonymized (names, affiliations, acknowledgements), contact the AC. Do not let authors’ identities influence decisions even if discovered accidentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material in PDF or ZIP. Reviewers' responsibility is to read and review the submission itself; looking at supplementary material is at reviewer discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because NeurIPS submissions are short, reviewers may wish to consult supplementary material before criticizing submissions for insufficient details, proofs, or experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety when executing submitted code and following links
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat submitted code and external links as potentially unsafe. Run untrusted code only in secure, isolated environments and be cautious with links that may log IP addresses or contain vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended execution environments: (1) inside a Docker container, (2) in a Virtual Machine (VirtualBox/VMware), or (3) on a network-isolated cloud instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page-limit compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to eight content pages (figures/tables included) in the NeurIPS submission style; extra pages allowed only for broader impact and references. Authors must use the NeurIPS 2020 LaTeX style file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are assigned submissions that violate the NeurIPS style or page limits (e.g., decreased margins or font size), notify the AC immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions identical or substantially similar to papers submitted/accepted/published elsewhere (or to other NeurIPS submissions) are dual submissions and should be deemed as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly can be dual submission. If you suspect dual submission, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content should be detailed and informative
rubrics_metrics.description: Make reviews as detailed and informative as possible; short, superficial reviews that venture uninformed opinions or guesses are worse than no review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review content is primary for decisions and for authors to improve. Provide detail so ACs, SACs, and program chairs can make informed decisions and authors can act on feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs and authors detect misunderstandings. Summaries may not provide new info to authors but are invaluable. See Examples of Review Content for acceptable forms of summaries and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work, including soundness of claims (theoretical grounding, empirical evaluation), significance and novelty, and relevance to the NeurIPS community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific strengths (e.g., correct methodology, compelling experiments, novel theoretical results). Cite relevant prior works precisely when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaknesses (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain limitations of the work along axes like correctness, significance, novelty, and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be detailed, specific, and polite. Avoid vague subjective complaints. Help authors understand your viewpoint and how to improve; remember not to review based on your personal interest but on scientific contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims and methods are correct and whether empirical methodology is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect claims or methodology are primary reasons for rejection. Be detailed and specific; thoroughly motivate criticisms so authors can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the clarity of exposition and whether the paper is well written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give examples of parts needing revision. A superbly written paper provides enough information for an expert reader to reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether the submission adequately discusses how it differs from previous contributions and whether the related work is due scholarship rather than a mere list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are excused for not knowing all non-refereed/very recent ArXiv work (papers <2 months before deadline considered contemporaneous). For accepted camera-ready versions, better comparisons are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether there are enough details to reproduce the major results of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not reproducible, list lack of reproducibility among the weaknesses. Consult supplementary material if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional feedback and questions (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any additional comments, suggestions for improvement, and questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this field to request clarifications (e.g., 'I would like to see results of experiment X' or 'Please include details about parameter settings used for experiment Y').

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (review form item) and scoring guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an Overall Score reflecting your assessment of the submission's contributions, using a 1-10 scale with verbal anchors (10 = Top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers; 1 = Trivial or wrong or already known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT adjust scores to match conference acceptance rates or assumed representativeness. Examples for intermediate scores (9: Top 15% accepted; 8: Top 50% accepted; 7: good accept; 6: marginally above threshold; 5: marginally below; 4: okay but reject; 3: clear reject; 2: strong reject; 1: trivial/wrong).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (review form item) and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Confidence score on a 1-5 scale indicating how certain you are about your assessment and familiarity with the submission's area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 = absolutely certain; 4 = confident but not absolute; 3 = fairly confident (math/details not carefully checked); 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with some central parts; 1 = educated guess, not in area or difficult to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact statement adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the authors have adequately addressed the broader impact of their work, including potential negative ethical and societal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must include a statement discussing both positive and negative outcomes. Mark Yes, No, or Only partially and evaluate adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag whether the submission raises potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, or data that create/reinforce unfair bias or have primary purpose of harm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain briefly if concerns exist. This flag is independent of the review rating. If AC shares concern, dedicated ethics reviewers may be assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you previously reviewed or area chaired this work
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether you have previously reviewed or area chaired a version of this work for another archival venue (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs contextualize your review; ACs have access to resubmission statements from authors which may be shared with reviewers as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to area chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Field for comments that should be kept confidential from the authors (e.g., explicit comparisons to other submissions or blunt criticisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this field for more bluntly stated criticisms or private comparisons. Do not include author identities if discovered; instead report per conflict rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read and (if appropriate) respond to each author response before decisions are made and update reviews to indicate whether they agree or disagree with the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore author responses. If your opinion remains the same, explain why specifically (not just 'I have read the author response and my opinion remains the same').

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion phase participation and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: After the author response phase, AC will initiate discussion; reviewers should participate to work toward consensus, especially for borderline or conflicting assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus is valuable though not mandatory. Consider others' backgrounds and be willing to change your mind if appropriate; if you disagree, justify your viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality evaluation and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: 'exceeded expectations', 'met expectations', and 'failed to meet expectations'; top reviewers receive registration awards and low scorers may not be invited in future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The top 8% highest-scoring reviewers are awarded free registrations; the next top 30% will have registrations reserved for them. Poor reviews may affect future invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and exemplars of review content
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines provide many concrete examples of contributions, quality assessments, clarity comments, originality, and significance drawn from past reviews to illustrate good review content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples as templates for constructive, specific, and well-justified review text. If citing existing work to justify comments, be precise and provide complete citations.
